text.p: Israel's Elbit Medical Imaging Ltd, a subsidiary of Elron Electronic Industries

Elbit Imaging, which controls three medical-imaging equipment companies, said the decline in revenues was due to the reduction of its stake in the Hungarian company Omker from January 1, 1996 to 44 percent.
As a result, it no longer reported Omker on a consolidated basis. In 1995, the company had contributed revenues of $47.2 million.
Elscint added that ultrasound equipment made a significant contribution to fourth-quarter earnings, which the company said was due to seasonal factors.
The unit's sales were virtually unchanged for the quarter and the year, but a spokesman said that was due to Elbit's ending a contract representing the Japanese company Aloka .
Overall, management attributed the fourth-quarter improvement to wider operating margins at its closely held Elbit Ultrasound unit, and to cost-cutting at Elscint Ltd and at Elbit Imaging itself.
Elbit Imaging was one of three companies created by a breakup of Elbit Ltd, which went into effect in November 1996.
